messages.author: 7c598f9d5aed052f
messages.subject: Translating from qplot to ggplot
parts:
I'm trying to visualize the results of a strategic game using R and ggplot2 (overkill but a good training ground for a novice, I thought).

The data are here:

> result1 <- read.csv( "ftp://godesberg.homelinux.net/result1.csv" )
> result1 <- result1[-1]
> teams <- unique( result1$Tm )

I get what I want (ugly, I know, just interim stage[1]) with

> library( ggplot2 )
> qplot( rnd, Equity, data = result1, fill = Tm, group = Tm )
+ geom_bar( stat = "identity", position = "dodge" )
+ scale_fill_hue( "Team Name", breaks = teams, labels = teams )
+ xlab("Game Round")

but I've spent hours now, using the online documentation and Hadley's book, trying to translate that into a set of ggplot commands / layers -- without success. I get bits and peices translated but not exactly what I have with the qplot command.

Would be extremely grateful for a pointer in the right direction!

Thanks,
Rainer

[1] Using lines instead of bars, and other columns instead of Equity, I get already quite far

messages.author: 936ef8c6d12fc338
messages.subject: RE: Translating from qplot to ggplot
parts:
This should do it

ggplot(data =result1, aes(x = rnd, y = Equity, fill = Tm)) + geom_bar(

stat = "identity", position = "dodge" ) +
scale_fill_hue( "Team Name", breaks = teams, labels =
teams ) +
xlab("Game Round")

Best regards,

Thierry

messages.subject: Re: Translating from qplot to ggplot
parts:
Ranier, 

I wouldn't suspect that 2.11.1 would be a problem. Usually when it's a problem is when someone says they're having problems on R 2.6 or something ridiculously out of date. My other machine is X86_64 and things usually run fine. 

I might have figured it out just now.

> > Error in +geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge") :
> >  invalid argument to unary operator

When you have another line make sure that the + goes at the end of the line and not at the beginning of the line. 

Example: 

ggplotobject +
xlab('X axis label')

NOT

ggplotobject
+xlab ('X axis label')

Does it work then?

Brandon
